h1: The 8 Best NAS Storage Devices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best NAS Storage Devices 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight diskless NAS boxes from Synology and UGREEN, from simple 2-bay backup hubs to 4-bay and 6-bay media servers.
summary: The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus is our pick for most buyers who want 4K transcoding power in a 4-bay box. The Synology DS925+ suits anyone who wants the newest DSM hardware, and the Synology DS223 is the cheapest way into a real NAS.
intro: The first NAS mistake is forgetting that every unit here ships empty. Drives are sold separately, so the price on the listing is only the start, and bay count decides how far that investment can grow.

We reviewed eight diskless NAS units from Synology and UGREEN and ranked them on bay count, processor, memory, software ecosystem and fit for a home or small office. Our source is the spec sheets and listing details only.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP4800 Plus
products.verdict: Four bays and a 5-core Intel chip aimed at 4K media.
products.description:
The DXP4800 Plus is a 4-bay diskless NAS built around an Intel Pentium Gold 8505 5-core processor. The listing positions it for strong 4K transcoding.

It beats the Synology DS925+ on listed processing power, while the Synology brings DSM software maturity. The DXP4800 GT adds more memory and an AMD chip.

Buy it if you stream and back up media at home. Remember drives are sold separately.

products.name: Synology DS925+
products.verdict: Synology's current-generation 4-bay with the DSM ecosystem.
products.description:
The DS925+ is a 4-bay diskless NAS running Synology's DSM software. The listing calls it the current-generation DiskStation.

It ranks below the DXP4800 Plus on listed hardware but gives you DSM and a longer support runway than older units like the DS425+.

Choose it if software polish and support matter most. Drives are sold separately.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prize DSM and support.
products.skipIf: You want the most CPU for the money.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP6800 Plus
products.verdict: Six bays and an Intel i3 for big libraries.
products.description:
The DXP6800 Plus is a 6-bay desktop NAS with an Intel i3 1215U 6-core CPU. It has the highest bay count and capacity ceiling in this guide.

It ranks third because most homes do not need six bays, but it beats the 4-bay models on growth room.

Buy it for large media libraries or a small office with several users. Drives are sold separately.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP4800 GT
products.verdict: The most RAM among 4-bay picks, on an AMD platform.
products.description:
The DXP4800 GT is a 4-bay desktop NAS with an AMD R2514 CPU and 8GB of DDR4 RAM, the most among the 4-bay picks here.

It ranks fourth because the Plus offers listed Intel transcoding focus, while the GT's extra memory helps multitasking.

Buy it if you run many services and are fine with AMD. Drives are sold separately.

products.name: Synology DS425+
products.verdict: A 4-bay Synology positioned as a private cloud media server.
products.description:
The DS425+ is a 4-bay diskless NAS with the DSM software ecosystem, positioned as a private cloud media server.

It ranks fifth because the DS925+ is the newer hardware, though both offer DSM.

Choose it if you want a private cloud. Drives are sold separately.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP4800 Pro
products.verdict: UGREEN's higher-tier 4-bay, with few details listed.
products.description:
The DXP4800 Pro is a 4-bay diskless NAS positioned as UGREEN's higher-tier 4-bay configuration.

It ranks sixth because the listing gives fewer specs than the Plus, so we can not confirm what the upgrade buys.

Buy it if you plan to grow into it. Confirm specs before ordering.

products.name: Synology DS225+
products.verdict: Two bays with an Intel CPU and hardware transcoding.
products.description:
The DS225+ is a 2-bay diskless NAS with an Intel CPU, hardware transcoding and DSM software.

It ranks seventh because two bays limit growth, though it costs less than the 4-bay units.

Buy it if you want DSM and transcoding without four bays.

products.name: Synology DS223
products.verdict: The simplest, cheapest real NAS here.
products.description:
The DS223 is a 2-bay diskless NAS positioned as a home and office backup hub, with DSM software.

It ranks last because it has the least headroom, but it is the cheapest true entry-level NAS in the group.

Buy it for simple backups. Drives are sold separately.

whatMatters.detail: Bays are the slots for hard drives. More bays allow more capacity and redundancy. Check the bay number in the title.
The CPU affects media transcoding and multitasking. Listed core counts help compare. Look for the model name.
RAM helps run many apps at once. Check the listed amount.
Synology DSM is the main software on those units. Software shapes daily use. Check what ecosystem is named.
Every NAS here ships without drives. Budget for them separately. Look for diskless in the title.

howToChoose.intro: Bays decide how far you can grow.

cards.label: Synology
cards.text: Synology offers the DSM ecosystem on the DS925+, DS425+, DS225+ and DS223.

cards.label: UGREEN
cards.text: UGREEN leans on hardware, with the DXP4800 Plus, GT, Pro and DXP6800 Plus.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers who value software should default to Synology.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: More bays, a stronger CPU and capacity to grow.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The UGREEN NAS DXP6800 Plus has the most bays, and the Synology DS925+ offers DSM on four.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You will grow, which favors the UGREEN NAS DXP4800 Plus or DXP6800 Plus.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only back up files, where the Synology DS223 is enough.

faq.q: Do these NAS units include hard drives?
faq.a: No. Every unit here is diskless, so drives are sold separately.

faq.q: What is the common NAS buying mistake?
faq.a: Counting only the box. Drives often cost as much as the NAS.

faq.q: Is a 4-bay NAS worth it over 2-bay?
faq.a: If you expect to expand, yes. For simple backup, the DS223 is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a NAS?
faq.a: Insert drives, connect to your network and follow the setup app.

faq.q: Do I need to maintain it?
faq.a: Update software, check drive health and keep backups.

faq.q: Can I stream media from it?
faq.a: Several are positioned for media, including the DXP4800 Plus and DS425+.

finalTake: The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus is the best fit for most home users. Choose the Synology DS925+ for software, and the DS223 for the lowest entry cost.
